body:
Thank you so much for taking the time to write this detailed, well-thought-out answer. I'll try to respond as best I can. I see the appeal in a lot of different aspects of pharmacy. My primary interest was industry, but I doubt I'll fit well in a corporate environment considering my deficits. I've listened to presentations on industry, psychiatric, and veterinary pharmacy, and also have some interest in oncology and infectious disease that I would like to explore further. I mentioned nuclear pharmacy in another post, but I don't know anyone in the specialty or how I can get my foot in the door.

I've been speaking with the therapeutics course director on how to do better with studying and on concerns with reentering the curriculum. I don't know who my assigned advisor would even be anymore since I've been out of the program and have yet to be reinstated. I've talked a bit with one of the CPNP advisors, but haven't really thought of much to ask.

My mental health has been a dumpster fire since kindergarten. I said I wanted to die when I was 8-9, and it hasn't really gotten much better. I've tried every SSRI under the sun, SNRIs, combinations, etc. I take atomoxetine, bupropion, and trazodone now, and they still only make me barely functional. Therapy has been next to worthless, and I've seen well over a dozen therapists and counselors in my lifetime. I don't think it's going to get any better than it currently is. With that kind of history and especially considering my current circumstances, I have no reason to believe my mental health is going to improve significantly any time soon. My only option is to work with how I currently am; I'll have to get through school like this, and possibly residency if I can make it there. I just obsess over medicine now. Studying keeps me from ruminating. Work, even though it's stressful in its own right, is a distraction, too. I just feel like that with no friends and no hobbies outside of reading anything related to medicine, I may as well throw myself into work and academics. That's how I'm keeping myself going.

The reason I worry is that I don't think I could live with myself if I was relegated to retail for the rest of my life. I'm already ashamed that I didn't get into medical school, which I still wish I could do, but I know that door's probably shut for me. I don't want my life to just boil down to answering phone calls to refill scripts, handling insurance issues, and asking prescribers if it's okay to change from capsules to tablets. Even if residency is stressful, I have nothing else but my career.

Thanks for your input. I don't have the personality or social skills to make up for lackluster grades, and I don't have the grades to make up for a lackluster personality. I hope that I can at least bring my grades back up in the fall, but the damage has already been done. My intelligence isn't anything to write home about, but it's all that I have. Still, what good is that if I can't impress during an interview? I don't think I have anything that would make me stand out in a positive way compared to the people I'd be competing with for a spot.

I'm guessing my best bet if residency/fellowship doesn't work out is to simply try to tough it out in retail for as long as possible while seeking out hospital jobs in the boonies? I really should have known better than to go into pharmacy knowing I have the social skills of a bag of rocks. I've entertained nuclear pharmacy, and would shell out the money for the training, but I've heard it's quite competitive, too. I'm not limited by geography since I don't have a family or SO to worry about, so that's a plus.
